scope: Named chestnut cultivars for zone 6b/7a sold as grafted, layered, tissue-culture or self-rooted trees, which come true to name: Chinese, Japanese, European, European × Japanese and complex hybrids, plus the Dunstan line, which is sold only as seedlings and tagged so. Seedlings grown from a named cultivar, unnamed seedlings, horse chestnut (Aesculus) and water chestnut are left out. Prices are for one grafted tree, the 2–4 ft size where a seller offers it. Every chestnut needs a second, pollen-producing tree nearby; pollen-sterile types are tagged.

varieties.name: Colossal
varieties.summary: The West Coast standard: very large, easy-peeling nuts, but it makes no pollen.
varieties.description: A European × Japanese hybrid long planted in California and the Pacific Northwest. Bears very large nuts (about 14–25 per pound) that drop early, in September to early October, and peel easily. It is pollen sterile, so it needs a pollen-producing chestnut such as Nevada nearby to set nuts.

varieties.name: Nevada
varieties.summary: The usual pollinator for Colossal; sweet, smaller nuts ripening late September.
varieties.description: A European-type chestnut grown mainly as the pollen partner for Colossal, which it blooms with. Its own nuts are sweet and starchy and ripen in late September. Sellers rate it hardy to about zone 4–5.

varieties.name: Bouche de Bétizac
varieties.summary: French hybrid with very large, early nuts; pollen sterile.
varieties.description: A French European × Japanese hybrid grown commercially in Europe for its very large, glossy nuts that ripen early. Like Colossal it produces no pollen, so plant it with a pollen-producing variety.

varieties.name: Marigoule
varieties.summary: French hybrid with large, sweet, easy-peeling nuts and good disease resistance.
varieties.description: A French European × Japanese hybrid valued for large, sweet nuts that peel easily, ripening mid-season. A good pollen producer, and sellers describe it as resistant to chestnut blight and phytophthora root rot. A vigorous, upright tree with good timber form; zone 5–8.

varieties.name: Précoce Migoule
varieties.summary: Early-ripening French hybrid with large nuts; produces pollen.
varieties.description: A French European × Japanese hybrid related to Marigoule, selected for early ripening. Bears large nuts and produces pollen, so it can pair with the pollen-sterile early types.

varieties.name: Belle Épine
varieties.summary: Late-ripening French chestnut with large nuts; a pollen producer.
varieties.description: A traditional French chestnut, sold in the US as a European × Japanese hybrid. Bears large nuts late in the season and produces pollen.

varieties.name: Maraval
varieties.summary: Vigorous, upright French hybrid with large, late nuts.
varieties.description: A French European × Japanese hybrid: a vigorous, upright tree bearing large nuts late in the season. A pollen producer. Usually sold layered (own-root) rather than grafted.

varieties.name: Marsol
varieties.summary: French European × Japanese hybrid with large nuts.
varieties.description: A French European × Japanese hybrid with large nuts, also widely used in Europe as a rootstock for other chestnuts.

varieties.name: Marrisard
varieties.summary: French European × Japanese hybrid.
varieties.description: A French European × Japanese hybrid selection with large nuts, offered grafted in several sizes.

varieties.name: Bergantz
varieties.summary: European × Japanese hybrid selection.
varieties.description: A European × Japanese hybrid selection, offered grafted or as seedlings.

varieties.name: Bisalta No. 2
varieties.summary: Italian-named European × Japanese hybrid.
varieties.description: A European × Japanese hybrid from the Bisalta series, named for the mountain near Cuneo in Italy's chestnut country.

varieties.name: Primato
varieties.summary: Italian European × Japanese hybrid.
varieties.description: An Italian European × Japanese hybrid chestnut, offered grafted or as seedlings.

varieties.name: Marron Comballe
varieties.summary: Traditional French marron (European chestnut).
varieties.description: A traditional French European chestnut sold as a marron, the name for large nuts with a single kernel that are prized for roasting and candying.

varieties.name: Marrone di Chiusa Pesio
varieties.summary: Italian marrone from Piedmont.
varieties.description: An Italian European chestnut of the marrone type, named for Chiusa di Pesio in Piedmont. Grown for large, single-kernel nuts.

varieties.name: Marrone di Val di Susa
varieties.summary: Italian marrone from Piedmont's Susa Valley.
varieties.description: An Italian European chestnut of the marrone type from the Susa Valley in Piedmont, grown for large, single-kernel nuts.

varieties.name: Marron de Goujounac
varieties.summary: French European marron.
varieties.description: A French European chestnut of the marron type, named for Goujounac in the Lot.

varieties.name: Judia
varieties.summary: Portuguese European chestnut.
varieties.description: A traditional Portuguese European chestnut cultivar, one of the main ones grown there for market.

varieties.name: Tanzawa
varieties.summary: Japanese chestnut with large, early nuts.
varieties.description: A Japanese chestnut (Castanea crenata) cultivar bearing large nuts early in the season. Japanese chestnuts have big nuts but a bitterer, harder-to-peel skin than European or Chinese types.

varieties.name: Tsukuba
varieties.summary: Japanese chestnut with large nuts; a leading cultivar in Japan.
varieties.description: A Japanese chestnut (Castanea crenata) cultivar widely grown in Japan for its large nuts and steady crops.

varieties.name: Okei
varieties.summary: Japanese chestnut cultivar.
varieties.description: A Japanese chestnut (Castanea crenata) cultivar with large nuts; also sold layered.

varieties.name: Torakuri
varieties.summary: Japanese-type chestnut with large nuts.
varieties.description: A Japanese-type chestnut cultivar (Castanea crenata hybrid) offered grafted in several sizes.

varieties.name: Silverleaf
varieties.summary: Japanese chestnut selection sold as Silverleaf or Eurobella.
varieties.description: A Japanese chestnut (Castanea crenata) selection, sold as Silverleaf or Eurobella, offered grafted or as seedlings.

varieties.name: Gillet
varieties.summary: Japanese-type hybrid selection.
varieties.description: A Japanese chestnut (Castanea crenata) hybrid selection, offered grafted.

varieties.name: Skioka
varieties.summary: Chinese × European hybrid.
varieties.description: A Chinese × European hybrid, combining Chinese chestnut's blight tolerance with European nut size. Offered grafted or as seedlings.

varieties.name: Layeroka
varieties.summary: Chinese × European hybrid.
varieties.description: A Chinese × European hybrid chestnut, offered grafted or as seedlings.

varieties.name: Szego
varieties.summary: Complex Japanese × Chinese × chinquapin hybrid.
varieties.description: A complex hybrid of Japanese and Chinese chestnut with chinquapin (Castanea pumila) in its background, offered grafted.

varieties.name: Sleeping Giant
varieties.summary: Big, sweet nuts on a tall timber-form tree; hardy to zone 4.
varieties.description: A hybrid of Chinese, Japanese and American chestnut, grown for big, sweet nuts on a tall, timber-form tree. Blight resistant and hardy in zones 4–8, but an unreliable pollen producer, so plant it with a good pollinator. Grafted trees bear in 3–5 years.

varieties.name: Gideon
varieties.summary: Chinese chestnut with medium-large, easy-peeling nuts; zone 4–8.
varieties.description: A Chinese chestnut with medium to large nuts that ripen early to mid-season and peel easily. Often paired with Qing for pollination. Hardy in zones 4–8.

varieties.name: Mossbarger
varieties.summary: Kentucky Chinese × American hybrid known for consistently large crops.
varieties.description: A Chinese × American hybrid from Kentucky, introduced in 1983 and selected for blight resistance. Bears large, sweet nuts early to mid-season. Zones 5–9.

varieties.name: Dunstan
varieties.summary: The best-known blight-resistant American × Chinese chestnut; sold as seedlings.
varieties.description: A blight-resistant American × Chinese chestnut line, sold as seed-grown trees from the patented Dunstan parent trees rather than as a grafted clone, so individual trees vary. Widely planted in the eastern US for nuts and wildlife; plant at least two for pollination. Zones 5–9.
